title: Sub-band scale-free test: is the TEP clock field scale-free?
interpretation: Sub-band lambda coefficient of variation = 0.414 (>= 0.20) — the correlation length VARIES with frequency. This is more consistent with an atmospheric/ionospheric interpretation (frequency-dependent processes) than with a scale-free TEP field.

For reference: tropospheric ZTD correlation ~500 km, ionospheric TEC correlation ~1000-2000 km, synoptic weather ~1000-3000 km. The measured clock correlation scale (3601.637138033869 km) is much larger than these atmospheric scales.
pre_registered_prediction: Under TEP, the clock correlation field should be scale-free within the 10-500 uHz band — the same correlation length in every sub-band.  Under an atmospheric/ionospheric interpretation, the correlation length should vary with frequency because different atmospheric processes dominate at different periods.  A coefficient of variation < 0.20 across sub-bands supports TEP; >= 0.20 supports atmospheric.
